task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		Your phone has been showing 'No Service' for the past few hours.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
I found the problem, John. Your number 555-123-2002 is on line L1002, and that line is currently **suspended**. The reason is an overdue bill:

- **Bill B1234321** — amount due **$65.00** (due date was 2025-01-15), status: Overdue.

I've sent a payment request to you for that bill. Please:
1. Check your payment requests using the **check_payment_request** tool.
2. Accept the payment request so I can process the $65.00 payment.

Once the payment goes through and the bill shows as Paid, I'll be able to lift the suspension on your line and get your service back. Let me know once you've accepted it, or if you'd like me to check the status again.
turns.execution_output: User: Oh dear, an overdue bill? I had no idea... Well, if that's what's causing it, I'll pay it. Let me check this payment request thing you sent me.

turns.thought:
Yes, it went through! Your payment of $65.00 was received, and bill B1234321 is now marked as **Paid**.

I've also lifted the suspension on your line — number **555-123-2002** (line L1002) is now **Active** again.

One last step on your end: please **reboot your phone** (power it off and back on). After it restarts, your service should come back and you should be able to make calls again.

Note: I did also see another bill, B1002 for $150.00, but it isn't due until 2025-02-19, so nothing is needed on that right now. Let me know if your service doesn't return after the reboot!

No, you didn't do anything wrong at all — this is a simple fix. What you're describing is **Airplane Mode** being turned on. Airplane Mode switches off all of your phone's wireless connections, including the cellular connection, which is why you see "No Service" and no signal bars. Your line itself is fine and active now.

Here's what to do:

1. **Swipe down from the very top of your screen** (do it twice if needed) to open the full quick settings panel.
2. Look for the **airplane icon (✈️)**. If it's highlighted/colored in, it's on.
3. **Tap the airplane icon** to turn Airplane Mode OFF.

If you'd rather do it through the settings menu:
- Open **Settings**
- Tap **Network & internet** (or "Connections" on some phones)
- Find **Airplane mode** and switch it **OFF**

If you have the option to run the **toggle_airplane_mode()** action on your device, you can use that to turn it off as well.

After you turn it off, wait about 30 seconds and the signal bars should come back. Give me a moment-by-moment update — if you still see no signal after that, tell me and we'll check further (we can look at your SIM, network settings, or do a reboot).
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me try that airplane thing... I'll tap the little airplane icon.

turns.thought:
You haven't broken anything — I promise. Let's take it one step at a time.

Here's what's going on: "No Signal" and "Data disabled" are two separate things, and the data part is just a switch on your phone. It's very common for Airplane Mode to turn mobile data off as well when it's switched on, so this is expected.

**Step 1 — Turn mobile data back ON**
1. Swipe down from the top of your screen again to open quick settings.
2. Look for the **Mobile data** (or "Cellular data") tile — it may have a small antenna/signal icon.
3. If it looks greyed out or says "Off," **tap it** to turn it ON.

Or through Settings:
- Open **Settings** → **Network & internet** (or "Connections")
- Tap **Mobile network** (or "SIMs")
- Switch **Mobile data** to ON

If you have the option to run **toggle_data()** on your device, that will do the same thing.

**Step 2 — Wait for the signal**
Once mobile data is on, give the phone about 30–60 seconds to reconnect to the network. Signal bars should reappear.

A quick note on your data: your line has used 8.7 GB out of 15 GB this cycle, so you have plenty of data left — this isn't a data limit issue at all.

Try Step 1 and let me know what the top of your screen shows afterward. If it still says "No Signal" after that, I'll walk you through checking the SIM card and APN settings next — both are easy fixes.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me turn that mobile data thing back on.

turns.thought:
I hear you, and I'm sorry this has taken so many steps — you've done everything right. Let's try the next fix, which is the most likely one here.

Your phone's **APN settings** (these tell the phone how to connect to our network) may have been reset or entered incorrectly. That causes exactly what you're seeing: no signal and data not connecting.

**Please do this:**

1. On your phone, run the **reset_apn_settings()** action — this restores your network settings to our defaults. (If you'd rather do it in menus: **Settings** → **Network & internet** → **Mobile network** → **Access Point Names (APN)** → tap the **⋮ menu** → **Reset to default**.)

2. After that, run **reboot_device()** to restart your phone. This step is required — the new settings won't take effect until the phone restarts.

3. Once it comes back on, wait about a minute and check the top of the screen.

If it still shows "No Signal" after the reboot, don't worry — we have more options, including checking your SIM card, and I can also get a specialist involved.

Just let me know what you see after the restart.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay... I'll try that reset thing. I just hope I don't lose my photos of the grandchildren.

turns.thought:
I completely understand your frustration, and I want to reassure you: **there's no sign your phone is broken.** I've re-checked your line and everything on our end looks correct — status Active, suspension cleared, contract valid, and you have 8.7 GB of 15 GB data used, so no limits are blocking you.

Let's do one more targeted check before I bring in extra help.

**Please run the following two checks on your phone:**

1. **check_sim_status()** — this tells us whether your SIM card is seated properly, missing, or locked.
2. **check_network_mode_preference()** — this shows whether your phone is set to an older network mode (like 2G/3G) that could prevent it connecting.

If you'd rather do these in your phone's menus:
- SIM: **Settings** → **About phone** → **SIM status**
- Network mode: **Settings** → **Network & internet** → **Mobile network** → **Preferred network mode** (it should say 5G/4G auto or similar)

Tell me what those two show. If the SIM comes back as "Missing", we can simply reseat it; if it's "Locked" or the checks don't resolve it, I'll transfer you straight to a human technical support agent who can take over from here with more advanced tools. You won't be left on your own.
turns.execution_output: User: I can only do one thing at a time, I'm afraid — all this is a bit much for me. Let me do the first one, the SIM card check.
